newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy "continues to hum," White House says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy "continues to hum," White House says.

text.p: Newly released figures on second-quarter national output show a steadily growing economy set to benefit from soaring business investment, White House Economic Adviser Janet Yellen said on Thursday.

"Today's GDP numbers suggest that the economy continues to hum: growth is robust, unemployment remains low at 5 percent, inflation is in check, household wealth is rising and consumer confidence surveys register record optimism," Yellen said.
Gross domestic product grew at 2.2 percent a year in the second quarter, down from 4.9 percent in the first quarter with price rises at the slowest rate since the 1960s.

Yellen said the government's budget deficit has fallen by more than 75 percent during the past four years under the Clinton administration and said that this has helped trigger strong growth in business investment at 11 percent a year.
"These soaring levels of business investment have contributed to our economy's current strength and are helping to lay foundations for future higher long-term economic growth," Yellen added.
